blocks.md: Three things stand between you and a training run: the hardware to do it, a dataset to learn from, and a validation set to measure progress against. Get these right and everything afterwards is mostly patience.

blocks.label: Label · The cloud alternative

blocks.label: Paragraph · If your card is too small, rent one. Services such as vast.ai a…
blocks.md: If your card is too small, rent one. Services such as [vast.ai](https://vast.ai) and [runpod.io](https://runpod.io) rent fast GPUs by the hour, and you can train on hardware you could never justify buying. The trade-off is setup overhead and the pressure of paying for every idle minute — see [Chapter 12](training.html#cloud).

blocks.label: Paragraph · The dataset is the part that takes longest, because it is mostl…
blocks.md: The dataset is the part that takes longest, because it is mostly research and file management rather than compute. You are hunting official stems across the internet and arranging them so the trainer can read them.

blocks.label: Label · Format rule
blocks.md: Format rule

blocks.label: Paragraph · Every track in your dataset must be FLAC or WAV. MP3 will not w…
blocks.md: Every track in your dataset must be **FLAC or WAV**. MP3 will not work — lossy compression changes the waveform enough that the model learns the codec's artefacts.

blocks.label: Subheading · If you have no dataset yet
blocks.md: If you have no dataset yet

blocks.label: Paragraph · Start with Bas Curtiz's walkthrough, which covers dataset creat…
blocks.md: Start with Bas Curtiz's walkthrough, which covers dataset creation in far more depth than a written chapter can: [youtube.com/watch?v=Wmt\_0zu94L8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wmt_0zu94L8). What follows is how that dataset must be laid out for this specific trainer.

blocks.label: Subheading · Type 1 — one folder per song, one file per stem
blocks.md: Type 1 — one folder per song, one file per stem

blocks.label: Paragraph · Type 1 mirrors the MUSDB18 structure and is what 4-stem models…
blocks.md: Type 1 mirrors the MUSDB18 structure and is what 4-stem models expect. Every stem of a song lives together, and **all stems of a song must end at the same time** — the trainer reads them as one aligned example.

blocks.label: Label · Mismatched stem lengths
blocks.md: Mismatched stem lengths

blocks.label: Paragraph · If stems differ in length you will hit this while the metadata…
blocks.md: If stems differ in length you will hit this while the metadata is being collected:

blocks.label: Paragraph · Trim or pad the offending stems so every file in the folder end…
blocks.md: Trim or pad the offending stems so every file in the folder ends on the same sample.

blocks.label: Subheading · Type 2 — one folder per stem, all songs inside
blocks.md: Type 2 — one folder per stem, all songs inside

blocks.label: Paragraph · Type 2 has exactly two folders: dump every instrumental into ot…
blocks.md: Type 2 has exactly two folders: dump every instrumental into `other` and every vocal into `vocals`. Track lengths *do not* need to match, because the loader picks random songs, splits each into chunks (exactly like an inference pass), mixes them and feeds the result to the model.

blocks.label: Label · Schematic · how the loader reads each layout
blocks.md: Schematic · how the loader reads each layout

blocks.label: Caption · Why the two layouts behave differently. Type 1 gives the model…
blocks.md: Why the two layouts behave differently. Type 1 gives the model one aligned song at a time, so the stems have to match sample-for-sample. Type 2 never sees a whole song: it draws random windows from each stem folder and mixes them, which is why track lengths can differ.

blocks.label: Subheading · How many files?
blocks.md: How many files?

blocks.label: Paragraph · The original documentation recommends at least 200 audio files…
blocks.md: The original documentation recommends **at least 200 audio files**, and more is always better. As a real reference point, the finished metal dataset in the source guide holds **2135 instrumentals and 1779 vocals** — 3914 tracks in total.

blocks.label: Card title · More tracks, more variety
blocks.md: More tracks, more variety

blocks.label: Paragraph · Standard 3–5 minute songs need volume: a few hundred tracks min…
blocks.md: Standard 3–5 minute songs need volume: a few hundred tracks minimum, ideally thousands. Breadth is what teaches a model to generalise.

blocks.label: Label · Long files
blocks.md: Long files

blocks.label: Card title · Fewer tracks, still long runs
blocks.md: Fewer tracks, still long runs

blocks.label: Paragraph · If your source material is 10 minutes or more per file, you can…
blocks.md: If your source material is 10 minutes or more per file, you can get away with a lower file count — the model still chunks the audio according to the `chunk_size` in your YAML.

blocks.label: Subheading · Where the audio should come from
blocks.md: Where the audio should come from

blocks.label: Paragraph · Use official sources. For vocals you can sometimes substitute a…
blocks.md: Use official sources. For vocals you can sometimes substitute a separation — a good Mel-Roformer pass, or inverting an official instrumental — but the recommendation stands: official instrumentals and official vocals give the cleanest training signal. Anything synthesised teaches the model the artefacts of whatever made it.

heading.label: Chapter heading · Building a validation set

blocks.label: Paragraph · The validation set is your scoreboard. It is small, it is read…
blocks.md: The validation set is your scoreboard. It is small, it is read after every epoch, and its only job is to tell you whether the model is actually improving.

blocks.label: Paragraph · For a Type 1 (4-stem) setup, each song folder also carries drum…
blocks.md: For a Type 1 (4-stem) setup, each song folder also carries `drums.wav` and `bass.wav`. The mixture is not an approximation — it is the stems summed, so the model's output can be compared directly against the truth.

blocks.label: Label · Schematic · validation/song name 1
blocks.md: Schematic · validation/song name 1

blocks.label: Caption · The relationship the metrics depend on. The model is asked to r…
blocks.md: The relationship the metrics depend on. The model is asked to reproduce `vocals` and `other` from `mixture`, so the three files have to describe exactly the same stretch of time. Shapes are illustrative, not real audio.

blocks.label: Label · 16-bit WAV only
blocks.md: 16-bit WAV only

blocks.label: Paragraph · The validation loader accepts 16-bit WAV files. Export them cor…
blocks.md: The validation loader accepts **16-bit WAV** files. Export them correctly: FLAC or 24-bit files can throw errors during validation, which is exactly the kind of problem you do not want to discover after a week of training.

blocks.label: Subheading · Choose your tracks wisely
blocks.md: Choose your tracks wisely

blocks.label: List item · Reuse tracks already in your dataset. You already have their st…
blocks.md: **Reuse tracks already in your dataset.** You already have their stems, so assembling the mixture and the folder is quick.

blocks.label: List item · Full tracks give higher metrics — more audio means a more repre…
blocks.md: **Full tracks give higher metrics** — more audio means a more representative score, and it is what the model will face in real use.

blocks.label: List item · Clips make validation faster. Cutting to 30 seconds–1 minute sp…
blocks.md: **Clips make validation faster.** Cutting to 30 seconds–1 minute speeds up every epoch, at the cost of lower metrics. That is a fine trade while you are testing a config and a bad one when you are judging a finished model.

blocks.label: Label · Everything must end at the same time
blocks.md: Everything must end at the same time

blocks.label: Paragraph · Inside each validation song folder, mixture, the stems and any…
blocks.md: Inside each validation song folder, `mixture`, the stems and any other files must be identical in length. If they are not, validation fails with a broadcast error:

blocks.label: Paragraph · Trim the longest file down, or re-export all of them from the s…
blocks.md: Trim the longest file down, or re-export all of them from the same edit session.
